grammar_focus: the choice of A or B / 省略关系词的定语从句(things you can do)、现在分词修饰名词(dogs barking incessantly)、最高级 the highest / even more + 比较级、被动多形式(be found to do / It was revealed that / be kept awake by)、whatever 引导让步 + pay for / against these figures(原创承载 NCE3 第三册 L47 考点·无需净化:污染题材科普——垃圾、食品与噪音污染,幽默揭出最古老的噪音源竟是打鼾;本课为轻松科普/幽默,无暴力,正常试读;美式化 garbage/cell phone/neighbor)
scene: 污染,就是我们为这个人口过密、过度工业化的星球付出的代价。当你静下来想一想,处理垃圾其实只有四种办法:倾倒、焚烧、变成可再利用的东西,或者设法少产生一些。这四种办法我们一直都在试,可全世界产生的垃圾,单是那庞大的数量就有把我们淹没的危险。然而,垃圾只是污染这个星球的一部分问题。对越来越多廉价食物的需求,导致了另一种污染。工业化的农作方式生产出廉价的肉类,而大量使用杀虫剂和化肥又生产出廉价的谷物和蔬菜。我们为廉价食物付出的代价,也许已经太高了。就算你打算戒掉肉类、改吃素,也只能二选一:要么选价格昂贵的有机蔬菜,要么每次以为自己在吃新鲜色拉时,其实都在不停地摄入杀虫剂。不过,还有一种更为隐蔽的污染,尤其侵扰城市、闯入我们的日常生活,那就是噪音。半夜响起的汽车警报,除了惹恼邻居别无用处。警笛和风镐在街上朝我们尖叫,是极度烦躁的来源。一项关于噪音影响的调查显示——也许出人意料——夜里不停吠叫的狗,在一到七的评分上被列为最严重的噪音污染。调查还列出了一长串人们真正讨厌的声音:夏日午后嗡嗡作响的割草机、公寓楼里的深夜派对、吵闹的邻居、轰隆隆穿过安静小镇的大集装箱卡车、头顶飞过的飞机和直升机,还有公共场所里开到最大音量的音乐。新技术也为噪音添了一份“贡献”。很多人反感手机,尤其是在餐馆或公共交通上使用时——大声的通话闯进我们的思绪,打断了和朋友安静聊天的乐趣。这项调查还揭示了一个相当出人意料、甚至有点好笑的老式噪音源。原来是打鼾!人们发现,男人是最厉害的“冒犯者”:据披露,三十五岁上下的男人有百分之二十打鼾,到了六十多岁,这个数字更是飙升到令人惊愕的百分之六十。与这些数字相比,只有百分之五的女性经常打鼾,其余的则不断被身边吹号般的伴侣吵醒、或搅得无法入睡。无论噪音来自何处,有一点是肯定的:寂静,似乎已成了一段珍贵的回忆。

grammar_card.title: the choice of A or B / 现在分词修饰名词 / 最高级·even more / 被动多形式 / whatever 让步
grammar_card.intro: ①the choice of A or B:在 A 和 B 之间选择;things (that) you can do 里关系词作宾语可省略。②现在分词短语放名词后修饰它,表主动:dogs barking incessantly。③the + 最高级表“最…”;even/still + more + 形容词表“更加…”。④被动多形式:be found to do(被发现…)、It was revealed that …(据披露…)、be kept awake by …(被…吵得睡不着)。⑤whatever + 名词引导让步:Whatever the source of noise, …;pay for(为…付出代价)、against these figures(与这些数字相比)。

rows: the choice of A or B
the choice of organic food or cheap food
even more + 形容词 / the 最高级
be found to do / It was revealed that
Men were found to be the worst

specialRules.rule: the choice of A or B 用 or 连接两项,不用 nor;of 不能换成 for。
whatever + 名词作让步状语(Whatever the source, …),不同于 however(接形容词/副词)、whenever(无论何时)。
美式:garbage/trash(英式 rubbish)、cell phone(英式 mobile)、neighbor(英式 neighbour)。本课已按美语写。

prelisten.q: Listen and answer — What does the writer describe as an 'amusing old-fashioned source of noise'?

passage: Pollution is the price we pay for an overpopulated, over-industrialized planet. When you stop to think about it, there are only four things you can do with garbage: dump it, burn it, turn it into something you can use again, or try to produce less of it. We keep trying all four methods, but the sheer volume of garbage we produce worldwide threatens to overwhelm us. Garbage, however, is only part of the problem of polluting our planet. The need to produce ever-larger quantities of cheap food leads to a different kind of pollution. Industrialized farming methods produce cheap meat, and the heavy use of pesticides and fertilizers produces cheap grain and vegetables. The price we pay for cheap food may already be too high. And if you think you will give up meat and become a vegetarian, you have the choice of either very expensive organically-grown vegetables or a steady diet of pesticides every time you eat what looks like a fresh salad. However, there is an even more insidious kind of pollution that especially affects urban areas and invades our daily lives, and that is noise. Car alarms going off in the middle of the night serve only to annoy the neighbors. Sirens and jackhammers scream at us in the street and are a source of profound irritation. A recent survey of the effects of noise revealed, perhaps surprisingly, that dogs barking incessantly at night rated the highest form of noise pollution on a scale ranging from one to seven. The survey turned up a long list of sounds that people really dislike: lawn mowers whining on a summer afternoon, late-night parties in apartment buildings, noisy neighbors, big container trucks thundering through quiet towns, planes and helicopters flying overhead, and loud music played at maximum volume in public places. New technology has made its own contribution to noise, too. Many people object to cell phones, especially when they are used in restaurants or on public transportation, where loud conversations invade our thoughts and interrupt the pleasure of a quiet chat with friends. The survey also revealed a rather surprising and possibly amusing old-fashioned source of noise. It turned out to be snoring! Men were found to be the worst offenders. It was revealed that twenty percent of men in their mid-thirties snore, and that this figure rises to a staggering sixty percent of men in their sixties. Against these figures, it was found that only five percent of women snore regularly, while the rest are constantly woken or kept awake by their trumpeting partners. Whatever the source of noise, one thing is certain: silence, it seems, has become a golden memory.

grammar_points.name: the choice of A or B / 省略关系词的定语从句
现在分词修饰名词(dogs barking incessantly)

被动多形式(be found to do / It was revealed that / be kept awake by)
whatever 引导让步 / pay for / against these figures

stage5.stem: "You have the choice ___ expensive organic food or cheap processed food."(the choice ___ A or B:在…之间选择,填介词)
stage5.stem_cn: 你可以在昂贵有机食品和廉价加工食品之间选择。

stage5.stem: "There are four things you can do ___ garbage."(处理某物 do sth ___,填介词)
stage5.stem_cn: 处理垃圾只有四种办法。

stage5.stem: "You can either recycle garbage ___ produce less of it."(either … ___ …:或者…或者)
stage5.stem_cn: 你要么回收垃圾,要么少产生垃圾。

stage5.stem: "Dogs ___ incessantly at night are the worst noise."(现在分词修饰 dogs:不停吠叫的)
stage5.stem_cn: 夜里不停吠叫的狗是最糟的噪音。

stage5.stem: "Car alarms ___ off at night annoy the neighbors."(现在分词修饰 alarms:响起的)
stage5.stem_cn: 半夜响起的汽车警报吵到邻居。

stage5.stem: "Lawn mowers ___ on a summer afternoon disturb everyone."(现在分词修饰 mowers:嗡嗡作响的)
stage5.stem_cn: 夏日午后嗡嗡作响的割草机搅得人人不安。

stage5.stem: "Noise is an even ___ insidious kind of pollution than garbage."(even + 比较级:更加…)
stage5.stem_cn: 噪音是比垃圾更隐蔽的一种污染。

stage5.stem: "Barking dogs rated the ___ form of noise pollution."(the + 最高级:最…的)
stage5.stem_cn: 吠叫的狗被评为最严重的噪音污染。

stage5.stem: "Men are the ___ offenders when it comes to snoring."(the + 最高级:最坏的)
stage5.stem_cn: 说到打鼾,男人是最厉害的“冒犯者”。

stage5.stem: "Men were ___ to be the worst offenders."(be ___ to be…,“被发现是”,填过去分词)
stage5.stem_cn: 人们发现男人是最厉害的打鼾者。

stage5.stem: "It ___ revealed that 20% of men snore."(被动 It ___ revealed that,据披露,填 be 动词过去式)
stage5.stem_cn: 据披露,百分之二十的男人打鼾。

stage5.stem: "Many women are kept awake ___ their snoring partners."(被动 + 施动者,填介词)
stage5.stem_cn: 许多女人被打鼾的伴侣吵得睡不着。

stage5.stem: "___ the source of noise, silence is now rare."(“无论噪音来自何处”,让步)
stage5.stem_cn: 无论噪音来自哪里,寂静如今都很难得。

stage5.stem: "Pollution is the price we pay ___ an industrialized world."(pay ___:为…付出代价,填介词)
stage5.stem_cn: 污染是我们为工业化世界付出的代价。

stage5.stem: "___ these figures, only 5% of women snore."(“与这些数字相比”:___ these figures)
stage5.stem_cn: 与这些数字相比,只有百分之五的女性经常打鼾。

stage5.stem: "Something harmful in a hidden, gradual way is ___."(“暗中为害的”用哪个词)
"To defeat or bury someone completely is to ___ them."(“制服、使不知所措”用哪个词)
stage5.stem_cn: 彻底压倒、使人不知所措。

stage5.stem: "A number so large it shocks you is ___."(“令人惊愕的”用哪个词)
